readiness.number: GA4: Demo page visitors 7d: 80 members for Display, used by the enabled campaign Display | Remarketing | Demo visitors

GA4 audiences can be used for remarketing.

readiness.number: 3 of 4 key events fired in 90 days; generate_lead is silent
readiness.why: sign_up (2,140) and demo_booked (310) can feed converter exclusions; generate_lead belongs to a retired contact form.

readiness.number: last 7 days hold 23.8% of the 30-day users
readiness.why: No recent change, so the pools are counts, not projections.

readiness.number: 1 of 3 browse and cart metrics tracked (Started Checkout)
readiness.why: Started Checkout fires when someone starts the sign-up form, so the abandoned sign-up flow can trigger; there is no Viewed Product, which a booking app doesn't need.

All users (540 days); Purchasers (540 days); Pricing visitors 30d (30 days); Demo page visitors 7d (7 days); Blog readers 90d (90 days). Pricing visitors 30d covers part of the Hot tier; none covers the sign-up and demo pages together.

readiness.number: 1 SIMILAR list still shows (Similar to all visitors)
readiness.why: Google retired similar segments; it is never planned with.

checks.evidence: TOF, MOF and BOF all run; no customer ad set (the customer list is only used as an exclusion)
10.4 on Retargeting | Pricing and sign-up page 14d
BOF takes 36.6% of funnel spend for 8.6% of the retargeting pools (4.3 times); its $110.00 a day is $3,300.00 a month against a spend ceiling of $2,142.82 for the Hot tier (Step 6)
Retargeting | All visitors 30d has no excluded_custom_audiences, so it pays to show sign-up ads to people who signed up and to customers
Prospecting | Broad | Salon and studio owners doesn't exclude Site visitors 30d
Demo page 7d: delivery_status 300 (too small); All visitors 180d: 180-day retention, longer than any tier's window; neither is used by an ad set

funnel_now.reading: Retargeting beats prospecting on cost: $38.41 a sign-up on BOF and $27.57 on MOF, against $47.63 on TOF. The problem is shape, not value: BOF is overfunded for its pool, so each person sees it 10.4 times a month.

pairs.pair: Abandoned sign-up flow and the BOF ad set (pricing and sign-up page 14d)
pairs.evidence: the flow's first email goes 1 hour after Started Checkout, and the BOF ad set can serve from the same visit; 960 people entered the flow in 30 days
pairs.fix: email first: hold paid until day 2 by excluding people who clicked an abandoned sign-up email in the last 24 hours, or set the BOF audience to start a day later

pairs.pair: Onboarding flow and the MOF ad set (all visitors 30d)
pairs.evidence: the onboarding flow mails everyone who signed up (2,050 in 30 days), and the MOF ad set excludes nobody, so new sign-ups keep seeing sign-up ads
pairs.fix: exclude Signed up 30d and Paying customers (list) from the MOF ad set (payload below)

pairs.evidence: 560 people saw the demo page in 30 days; no flow can reach them (they haven't given an email), the BOF rule covers only /pricing and /signup, and the Google demo list is too small to serve
pairs.fix: add /demo to the Hot audiences on Meta and Google

pairs.evidence: 140 lapsed customers entered win-back in 30 days; no ad set targets them after the last email
pairs.fix: a small customers tier on Meta and Google from the cancelled list, after the flow ends

email_and_paid_overlap.note: This overlap is structural: the same trigger in the same days. Neither platform reports how many of the same people both reached.

meta.audience_rules: website audiences: URL contains the tier's paths; retention 30 days (Hot also gets /demo)
meta.exclusions: Signed up 30d and Paying customers (list) on every retargeting tier, plus each hotter tier; prospecting excludes Site visitors 30d
meta.frequency: held by budget and audience size; Meta caps frequency only on reach-optimised ad sets

google_ads.campaign_type: Display, with the GA4 tier audiences as targeting
google_ads.list_source: GA4 audiences (the link has personalised ads on)
google_ads.frequency: set the Display frequency cap to each tier's per-day figure

budget.basis: the $4,170.00 your Meta retargeting ad sets spent in the last 30 days, split by tier
budget.by_phase: about 50% in days 1-7, 30% in days 8-14, 20% in days 15-30
budget.ceiling_math: pool x weekly cap x 4.3 x CPM / 1,000, at the retargeting ad sets' 30-day CPM of $20.34 (205,000 impressions)
budget.finding: The Hot ceiling is $2,142.82 a month, and BOF's $110.00 daily budget is $3,300.00 a month. Cut it to the Hot share, at most $2,085.00 (50% of today's retargeting spend); the shares then put $1,251.00 to $1,459.50 on Warm, well under its $4,285.64 ceiling.

kpis.basis: from your own history: retargeting should beat prospecting's $47.63 a sign-up
monitor: frequency daily: above 4 a week on Cool, refresh the creative
CTR weekly: below 0.2%, change the message or the creative
conversion rate weekly: if it falls, check the sign-up page
CPM weekly: rising on a flat audience means fatigue
cost per sign-up weekly: above $47.63, cut the tier back or pause it

launch_checklist: Swap the Google Display list for the 30-day pricing list (the readiness fail)
Build the Hot and Warm GA4 audiences and the matching Meta website audiences, with /demo in Hot
Add the converter exclusions to the MOF ad set and the site-visitor exclusion to broad prospecting
Lower the BOF budget to the Hot ceiling and move the rest to Warm
Hold paid for a day after the abandoned sign-up email
Launch Hot first, then Warm and Cool after 3 to 7 days
Check the exclusions after the first week; refresh creative every 2 to 3 weeks
unknowns: How many people the email flows and the ads both reached: neither platform reports it, so the overlap is structural.
Meta audience overlap between MOF and BOF: not in the API; check Audience Overlap in Ads Manager.
